name: Espresso
lede: Espresso is a very dark, reddish brown named for the coffee drink, close to black at a glance and warmer once it sits beside black.

sections.title: A drink, not a pigment
sections.body:
None of the 29 books we searched treats *espresso* as a color [1]. Finlay uses the word only for a coffee he drank in a Spanish café while looking for saffron fields [1]. The origin of the color name is undocumented in our sources [1][2].

Measured against the ISCC-NBS categories, the swatch is nearest to dark grayish reddish brown, 4.1 units of ΔE2000 away [2]. For neighbors see [[coffee]], [[dark-brown]] and [[chocolate-brown]].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This dark appears in 1,391 paintings in our archive, 5.85 per cent, as photographed [3]. John Singer Sargent has 19 of 287 paintings in it and Caravaggio 9 of 47 [3]. By century it peaks in the 1500s, in 194 of 2,231 paintings, 8.7 per cent [3]. Darkened varnish can push old paintings toward very dark browns, and these are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a color match is not a pigment test [3].
